title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 317
paragraphs: Therefore, passing these by, I shall make mention of the king who came after these, whose name was Sesostris. He (the priests said) first of all set out with ships of war from the Arabian gulf and subdued those who dwelt along the shores of the Erythraean Sea, until as he sailed he came to a sea that could no longer be navigated by reason of shoals. Then, after he had returned to Egypt, according to the priests' report, he took a great army and marched over the continent, subduing every nation that stood in his way. Those whom he found valiant and fighting desperately for their freedom — in their lands he set up pillars that told by inscriptions his own name and the name of his country, and how he had subdued them by his power. But as to those whose cities he obtained possession of without fighting or with ease, on their pillars he inscribed words of the same tenor as those for the nations that had shown themselves courageous, and in addition he carved on them the hidden parts of a woman, wishing to signify by this that the people were cowards and effeminate.
